scope: Development diagnostics for fixed tiny synthetic models; no acceptance qualification.
metrics_scope: Each step retains every role's tensor-gate summary and, separately, metrics for concatenating all tensors in that role. Maximum tensor relative L2 is not concatenated role relative L2.
missing_evidence_scope: Missing evidence is represented explicitly and is never counted as passed.

historical_full_matrix.scope: The original full matrix remains the acceptance denominator; these diagnostics do not replace or rewrite it.

runtime_and_sources.scope: Observed package versions and matching Python wrappers do not establish compiled binary build provenance.

optimizer_probe_identity.scope: Actual optimizer classes and loaded binary hashes apply only to this routing probe. Runtime files were hashed in that execution and were not re-read on the review host. Loaded binary identity does not attest a public-source build or establish historical optimizer identities.

repeated_and_masked_controls.scope: Identical text controls are compared using storage dtype and bytes, including signed zero. Masked controls are separate inputs.

loss_semantics.scope: Recompute shifted, masked, globally normalized FP64 CE from each side's own captured logits. Scalar agreement is approximate and does not certify backward normalization.

native_noninterference.scope: Native equality across arithmetic controls shows reference changes did not alter these native captures; repeated native arrays are not independent samples.

operator_findings.scope: Local forward and backward controls on inspected development seeds; not calibration, held-out validation, or end-to-end qualification.
operator_findings.extended_ce_scope: Extended operator CE checks a local masked sum; it does not validate token shifting or global microbatch normalization.
operator_findings.fp64_raw_retention: The earlier operator capture downcast its FP64 raw arrays. The corrected capture preserves FP64 and inputs; prior evidence is unchanged.

first_attention_localization.scope: Earliest observed difference is the first attention core after equal observed Q/K/V inputs. Native internal instructions are unobserved; counterfactuals do not prove a kernel cause.

adamw_own_state_replay.scope: Every side is replayed from its own gradients and prior captured master/moments. No formula-residual gate is applied.
adamw_own_state_replay.scalar_scope: Only hyperparameter preparation changes. Explicit array operations do not emulate CUDA FMA, instruction order, or fused master subtraction.
adamw_own_state_replay.identity_scope: Historical optimizer class and binary identity were not captured. A later identity probe can establish its own execution only.

routing_first_step.scope: Step zero only. Independent routing choices are observed without forcing routes; exposure associations are not causal decompositions.

routing_all_steps.scope: All three captured steps, layers, samples, and tokens. Each side uses its own inputs and effective gate weights. Routing exposure is observational, not causal attribution or acceptance qualification.

development_matrix.scope: The full declared development matrix contains two cases across 64 world-size-eight topologies per model: 256 requested rows and 128 required rows across both models. Pending means a final result is unavailable; completion does not mean numerical acceptance.

prepared_fixtures.scope: Ten new synthetic fixtures were generated for declared calibration and held-out partitions. No model forward, routing inspection, calibration, or held-out evaluation was performed; geometry remains three steps with text64 and masked65 cases.

public_arithmetic_gpu_equivalence.scope: Exact public helper source and canonical storage bytes are compared with the earlier scoped GPU controls. Reproducing those observations does not establish numerical acceptance.

tp2_row_projection_probe.scope: Step-zero TP2 row projections on captured local operands. Formula metrics use the independent rounded formula as reference and the returned native output as candidate. Interpretation requires all 708 training observations to remain byte-identical.
tp2_row_projection_probe.limits: Neither GEMM accumulators nor pre-allreduce GEMM outputs were captured. FP64 products and their rounded FP32 variants do not emulate the unknown GPU reduction schedule. Scope is two layer-zero sites in the W2 TP2 SP-off fixture; no acceptance gate is selected.

gradient_normalization_probe.scope: Actual post-reduction dense and expert DDP buffer scaling in the masked65 W8 TP2 CP2 EP2 SP-on PP2 ETP1 fixture. Buffers include padding and unowned slots; this is not a proof of the complete backward graph. Interpretation requires all 1428 canonical training observations to remain byte-identical.
gradient_normalization_probe.formula_scope: Independently multiply each captured FP32 buffer value by its observed FP32 scaling factor in FP64, then round to FP32. The expected factor is FP32(1 / (683 * 2)).

adamw_first_step_update_sensitivity.scope: All parameter elements at step zero of the existing dense and MoE FA2 text controls. The design was frozen before this diagnostic opened captures, after earlier development analysis. This is descriptive development evidence, not calibration or held-out validation; no new threshold is selected.
adamw_first_step_update_sensitivity.criterion_scope: Counts refer only to abs(native stored update - reference stored update) > 3e-6, the original update max-absolute component. The event is not the complete policy decision. All original gates and elements remain in place.
adamw_first_step_update_sensitivity.formula_scope: Each side uses its own captured gradient and initial FP32 master. side_scalars_fp64 and side_scalars_fp32 use nominal reference scalars and FP32-prepared native scalars; both_nominal_fp64 uses nominal scalars on both sides. Each formula retains FP32 master/update storage rounding. No formula residual gate is applied.
adamw_first_step_update_sensitivity.near_zero_scope: The two fixed descriptive cutoffs are epsilon and ten times epsilon. Counts are marginal, intersection and union counts within each stated cohort; they are not new acceptance thresholds. Six sign classes distinguish exact zero, including its sign bit.
adamw_first_step_update_sensitivity.limits: Fresh moments are assumed zero by the frozen step-zero contract, not separately observed before the step. Captured gradients are inputs, not certified correct. Sign associations do not establish why gradients differ. Explicit arithmetic does not emulate all CUDA FMA or approximate functions, and does not qualify later momentum trajectories. Runtime-only artifacts were not rehashed on the review host.

gradient_collective_probe.scope: Slime communication-wrapper arguments for synchronous two-rank FP32 SUM bucket reduce-scatter, and locally owned outputs after the original synchronous coalescing-wrapper call returns, in the masked65 W8 TP2 CP2 EP2 SP-on PP2 ETP1 fixture. Coverage includes every dense/expert bucket, eight ranks and three steps. Complete paired noninterference requires all 1428 canonical observations to remain dtype-and-byte identical.
gradient_collective_probe.formula_scope: Independently add both captured FP32 participant inputs in FP64 and round once to FP32. Separately check bucket pre-scaling and replay from the original pre-sync inputs. Parameter and padding intervals, subnormal counts and signed-zero byte differences remain explicit.
gradient_collective_probe.limits: The exact pinned Slime wrapper source is verified. Its underlying closure function was not directly captured, and actual runtime Torch c10d function source was not verified. NCCL internal dispatch, instructions or flush-to-zero policy, other group sizes, asynchronous or AVG paths, other collectives and the complete backward graph are unobserved. Callable metadata is omitted; published source hashes identify the frozen probe and pinned Megatron files only. No new tolerance or acceptance gate is selected.
gradient_collective_probe.counts_scope: collective_groups counts bucket/step peer-group observations, not distinct NCCL communicators. Each owned-shard observation belongs to one participant. Participant input subnormal counts repeat in both peer output rows. Signed-zero counts measure expected-versus-observed differences.
